score: 33/100 simplified with every protected table proved or unchanged, 0 wrong; 35% of the reference reduction; the search fails on 13 of 43 Fivetran pipelines
metric: Pipelines adapted from public projects, with protected tables that must keep their names and exact output: KumoSQL's Refactor search returns its simplest pipeline, scored by kumosql.formatting.pipeline_complexity. 55 sqlglot optimizer fixtures split into 2 to 4 tables (reference: sqlglot's own simplified query), 43 Fivetran dbt packages of 18 to 49 tables and 2 jaffle_shop cases (reference: dead and pass-through tables removed). Quality is (original - output) / (original - reference), averaged over the 81 cases whose reference is simpler; a failed search counts 0.
correctness: 0 wrong: every output's protected tables agree with the original on 100 random and targeted DuckDB databases (optimizer off), the project's own seed rows and every trap witness; 2 outputs are proved by prove_models and 85 leave each protected table and everything it reads unchanged; 13 searches failed and count as not improved. The 55 dev sqlglot cases carry 24 traps, each with a witness.
held_out: 28 cases (21 sqlglot, 1 jaffle_shop, 6 Fivetran), run once: 7/28 simplified, 0 wrong, 1 search failure (memory)
caveats: Adapted, not original, cases: sqlglot (MIT, commit bffcdefc16b0) and dbt-labs/jaffle_shop_duckdb and seven Fivetran packages (Apache-2.0, pinned commits); licences in benchmarks/table_minimization/licenses. Fivetran references are mechanical (dead and pass-through tables removed), so they are targets, not optima. On the Fivetran pipelines the search ran out of memory on 11 cases (5 GB per case) and over 300 s on 2; it was run one case per process with those limits. Fivetran SQL was adapted: current_timestamp fixed, unordered STRING_AGG/ARRAY_AGG given an order, CTEs that shadow their own table renamed.
usefulness: 33/100 dev cases improved: sqlglot 3/55 (quality 0.05; the search inlines into derived tables, which scores higher than merging), jaffle_shop 1/2 (beats the reference), Fivetran 29/43 (quality 0.59, all by dropping unread tables); Fivetran complexity 11,717.5 -> 7,201.5 against 6,098.0 for the references
performance: sqlglot and jaffle_shop: median 0.5 s per case, 55 s in total (4 workers). Fivetran: median 64 s per case, max 300 s, 2,747 s in total for the cases that finished; checking 347 s.
